children.text: A ring of radius R in the xy plane has uniform positive line charge λ. A positive ion of charge Q and mass m is close to its centre. Ignore radiation. For dynamic trapping take λ=λ0+u cosΩt. In B, a trapped atom has transition energy ℏωA, excited lifetime τ and line half-width Γ estimated by energy-time uncertainty. Two counterpropagating lasers of frequency ωL slightly below ωA drive absorption at rate \(s(\omega)=s_L+\alpha(\omega-\omega_L)\) in the atom frame. Work to first order in v/c and assume m≫ℏωA/c² and sL≪αωL. An absorbed photon is re-emitted with nearly the same atom-frame frequency, with equal probability in either x direction. Use mH=\(1.674\times10^{-27}\) kg, e=\(1.602\times10^{-19}\) C, ε0=\(8.854\times10^{-12}\) F/m, kB=\(1.381\times10^{-23}\) J/K and ℏ=\(1.055\times10^{-34}\) J s.

statement.text:
Trapping ions and cooling atoms
A ring of radius R in the xy plane has uniform positive line charge λ. A positive ion of charge Q and mass m is close to its centre. Ignore radiation. For dynamic trapping take λ=λ0+u cosΩt. In B, a trapped atom has transition energy ℏωA, excited lifetime τ and line half-width Γ estimated by energy-time uncertainty. Two counterpropagating lasers of frequency ωL slightly below ωA drive absorption at rate \(s(\omega)=s_L+\alpha(\omega-\omega_L)\) in the atom frame. Work to first order in v/c and assume m≫ℏωA/c² and sL≪αωL. An absorbed photon is re-emitted with nearly the same atom-frame frequency, with equal probability in either x direction. Use mH=\(1.674\times10^{-27}\) kg, e=\(1.602\times10^{-19}\) C, ε0=\(8.854\times10^{-12}\) F/m, kB=\(1.381\times10^{-23}\) J/K and ℏ=\(1.055\times10^{-34}\) J s.

a-1a. Central electric field
Find the field to first order in x/R,y/R,z/R.
a-1b. Static stable frequencies
Identify stable directions and their small-oscillation angular frequency.
a-2. Alternating-field parameters
For \(\ddot z=(k^2+a\Omega^2\cos\Omega t)z\), find k and a.
a-3a. Fast component equation

Assume a≪1, Ω≫k and aΩ²≫k². Write z=p+q, with slowly varying p and small zero-mean rapidly varying q. Obtain the leading equation for q.
a-3b. Micromotion solution
Choose integration constants consistent with small zero-mean q and solve.
a-4a. Averaged slow motion
Find the effective equation for p.
a-4b. Dynamic stability
Find the condition for stable slow motion.
a-5. Radiofrequency threshold
Use λ0=\(8\times10^{-9}\) C/m, R=0.10 m, Q=e and m=100mH. Calculate k and the limiting Ω for a=0.04.
b-1. Lifetime width
Estimate Γ from energy-time uncertainty.
b-2a. Absorption and momentum rates

For v>0 define + as the beam coming towards the atom from +x and − as the beam arriving from −x. Calculate s± and signed momentum rates π± in the atom frame.
b-2b. Doppler friction
Find the laboratory force in terms of v,kL=ωL/c,ℏ and α under the stated small-sL approximation.
b-3. Recoil heating
An atom initially at rest absorbs and re-emits one photon each τ. List the two final momentum outcomes and find mean heating power.
b-4. Cooling equilibrium
Calculate the signed mechanical cooling power, equilibrium ⟨v²⟩ and temperature.
b-5. Temperature estimate
For m=100mH, ωL=\(2\times10^{16}\) rad/s, τ=\(5\times10^{-9}\) s and α=4, estimate T.

children.text: On axis the ring charge 2πRλ gives \(E_z=\lambda Rz/[2\epsilon_0(R^2+z^2)^{3/2}]\simeq\lambda z/(2\epsilon_0R^2)\). Symmetry and ∇·E=0 then give \[\mathbf E=\frac\lambda{4\epsilon_0R^2}(-x,-y,2z).\]
For Qλ>0, x and y are restoring while z is unstable. Thus \(\omega_x=\omega_y=\sqrt{Q\lambda/(4\epsilon_0R^2m)}\). The static ring cannot confine all directions.
Compare coefficients with QEz/m: \(k=\sqrt{Q\lambda_0/(2\epsilon_0R^2m)}\), \(a=Qu/(2\epsilon_0R^2m\Omega^2)\). The field checks a.
On a fast cycle freeze p, neglect its acceleration and the small q in the driving force. Then \(\ddot q=pa\Omega^2\cos\Omega t\).
Integration gives \(q=-pa\cos\Omega t+c_1t+c_2\). Bounded micromotion requires c1=0 and zero mean requires c2=0, so \(q=-pa\cos\Omega t\).
Substitute q and average, using ⟨cosΩt⟩=0 and ⟨cos²Ωt⟩=1/2. This gives \(\ddot p=(k^2-a^2\Omega^2/2)p\).
The coefficient must be negative: \(a^2\Omega^2/2>k^2\), or Ω>√2 k/|a|. For a>0 this is Ω>√2 k/a. Equality is marginal, not a restoring oscillation.

\(k=\sqrt{e\lambda_0/(2\epsilon_0R^2\,100m_H)}\simeq2.08\times10^5\,\mathrm{rad/s}\). Thus Ωmin≈\(7.35\times10^{6}\) rad/s, rounded in the source to \(7\times10^{6}\) rad/s. This is angular frequency, corresponding to about 1.17 MHz.
Use ΔE τ≈ℏ and ΔE=ℏΓ, giving Γ≈1/τ in the source width convention. Factors associated with precise linewidth definitions are outside this estimate.

The frequencies are \(\omega_\pm=\omega_L(1\pm v/c)\), so \(s_\pm=s_L\pm\alpha\omega_Lv/c\). With k±=ω±/c, \(\pi_+=-\hbar k_+s_+\) and \(\pi_-=+\hbar k_-s_-\). Re-emission has zero mean momentum in this frame.

Adding momentum rates and retaining first-order terms gives \(-2\hbar k_L^2\alpha v[1+s_L/(\alpha\omega_L)]\). Neglect the bracket correction. To this order the lab force is \(F=-2\alpha\hbar k_L^2v\).

For incoming momentum +ℏkL, the final momentum is 0 or 2ℏkL with equal probability. The mean kinetic gain is ℏ²kL²/m. Thus \(P_{in}=\hbar^2k_L^2/(m\tau)\). The opposite incident direction gives the same energy.

\(P_{cool}=Fv=-2\alpha\hbar k_L^2v^2\). Balance the mean against recoil heating to obtain \(\langle v^2\rangle=\hbar/(2\alpha m\tau)\). One-dimensional equipartition gives \(T=\hbar/(2\alpha k_B\tau)=\hbar\Gamma/(2\alpha k_B)\). The field checks T.
Substitution gives T≈\(1.91\times10^{-4}\) K, about 0.2 mK. Mass and laser frequency cancel in this simplified balance.

solution.text:
Trapping ions and cooling atoms
a-1a. Central electric field
On axis the ring charge 2πRλ gives \(E_z=\lambda Rz/[2\epsilon_0(R^2+z^2)^{3/2}]\simeq\lambda z/(2\epsilon_0R^2)\). Symmetry and ∇·E=0 then give \[\mathbf E=\frac\lambda{4\epsilon_0R^2}(-x,-y,2z).\]
a-1b. Static stable frequencies
For Qλ>0, x and y are restoring while z is unstable. Thus \(\omega_x=\omega_y=\sqrt{Q\lambda/(4\epsilon_0R^2m)}\). The static ring cannot confine all directions.
a-2. Alternating-field parameters
Compare coefficients with QEz/m: \(k=\sqrt{Q\lambda_0/(2\epsilon_0R^2m)}\), \(a=Qu/(2\epsilon_0R^2m\Omega^2)\). The field checks a.
a-3a. Fast component equation
On a fast cycle freeze p, neglect its acceleration and the small q in the driving force. Then \(\ddot q=pa\Omega^2\cos\Omega t\).
a-3b. Micromotion solution
Integration gives \(q=-pa\cos\Omega t+c_1t+c_2\). Bounded micromotion requires c1=0 and zero mean requires c2=0, so \(q=-pa\cos\Omega t\).
a-4a. Averaged slow motion
Substitute q and average, using ⟨cosΩt⟩=0 and ⟨cos²Ωt⟩=1/2. This gives \(\ddot p=(k^2-a^2\Omega^2/2)p\).
a-4b. Dynamic stability
The coefficient must be negative: \(a^2\Omega^2/2>k^2\), or Ω>√2 k/|a|. For a>0 this is Ω>√2 k/a. Equality is marginal, not a restoring oscillation.
a-5. Radiofrequency threshold
\(k=\sqrt{e\lambda_0/(2\epsilon_0R^2\,100m_H)}\simeq2.08\times10^5\,\mathrm{rad/s}\). Thus Ωmin≈\(7.35\times10^{6}\) rad/s, rounded in the source to \(7\times10^{6}\) rad/s. This is angular frequency, corresponding to about 1.17 MHz.
b-1. Lifetime width
Use ΔE τ≈ℏ and ΔE=ℏΓ, giving Γ≈1/τ in the source width convention. Factors associated with precise linewidth definitions are outside this estimate.
b-2a. Absorption and momentum rates
The frequencies are \(\omega_\pm=\omega_L(1\pm v/c)\), so \(s_\pm=s_L\pm\alpha\omega_Lv/c\). With k±=ω±/c, \(\pi_+=-\hbar k_+s_+\) and \(\pi_-=+\hbar k_-s_-\). Re-emission has zero mean momentum in this frame.
b-2b. Doppler friction
Adding momentum rates and retaining first-order terms gives \(-2\hbar k_L^2\alpha v[1+s_L/(\alpha\omega_L)]\). Neglect the bracket correction. To this order the lab force is \(F=-2\alpha\hbar k_L^2v\).
b-3. Recoil heating
For incoming momentum +ℏkL, the final momentum is 0 or 2ℏkL with equal probability. The mean kinetic gain is ℏ²kL²/m. Thus \(P_{in}=\hbar^2k_L^2/(m\tau)\). The opposite incident direction gives the same energy.
b-4. Cooling equilibrium
\(P_{cool}=Fv=-2\alpha\hbar k_L^2v^2\). Balance the mean against recoil heating to obtain \(\langle v^2\rangle=\hbar/(2\alpha m\tau)\). One-dimensional equipartition gives \(T=\hbar/(2\alpha k_B\tau)=\hbar\Gamma/(2\alpha k_B)\). The field checks T.
b-5. Temperature estimate
Substitution gives T≈\(1.91\times10^{-4}\) K, about 0.2 mK. Mass and laser frequency cancel in this simplified balance.
